newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack squeezed up in stock shortage.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack squeezed up in stock shortage.

text.p: Shares in Railtrack Plc surged to a record high on Friday as continued investment demand caught some market-makers short of stock, traders said.
Railtrack shares were up 24-1/2p at 378-1/2 by 1030 GMT, surpassing the previous record of 357p set Wednesday. "The stock has just been unbelievable," said one senior trader.

The stock earlier reached a high of 380p, some 33 percent above its close of 285p on November 14. "One broker marked it up sharply higher at the outset, suggesting he could have been a bit short," said another trader.

Railtrack received a boost this week as analysts at NatWest Securities raised profit forecasts for the operator of the UK rail network. The stock has also been boosted since its flotation in May by hopes of a revaluation of its property portfolio.

Yet other utilies have also been strong this week amid talk that some investors were seeking high-yield shares ahead of a period of likely market uncertainty, with Chancellor Kenneth Clarke due to present his budget next Tuesday.
National Power Plc reached a four-month high of 468p and was up 14p at 466 by 1049 GMT, extending Thursday's 17p gain.
British Energy was up 16-1/2p at 151, after also setting a post-privatisation high of 153-1/2, amid positive press comment on yesterday's first-half results.
"Energy and Railtrack have really hoofed it," said one trader, "perhaps people seeking safe high yield stocks ahead of a period of uncertainty."
